result.reason: Clarity: B is built for a phone reader — subject line, four labeled sections, two-to-three-sentence paragraphs — while A is four dense blocks that pack net, gross, index, YTD and since-inception returns into one opening paragraph. B also translates jargon instead of restating it ("we moved to bonds that mature sooner, so that money comes due closer to when you will need to withdraw it"), whereas A's explanation of the duration change ("helps match the withdrawal schedule more closely to market conditions") is circular and conveys nothing to a layperson. B pre-empts obvious questions by flagging $19,200 as half the required amount and promising follow-up on the remainder, and it explains the ten-year rule before citing the 2034 date; A leaves both gaps. Tone: B sequences the sensitive fee increase well — reason, then rate, then notice — and closes with "please call me with any questions, including about the fee change," the right posture for a bereaved beneficiary facing a higher rate. A never invites that conversation, attaches "we are pleased to report" to a defensive portfolio change, and uses template filler ("this important chapter of your financial life") that reads impersonally given the circumstances. A's genuine edge is the salutation: "Dear Ines" is correct for a single named beneficiary, while B's "Dear Castellanos-Weir Household" is a mail-merge artifact and the wrong register; "nothing is left stranded" is also slightly clipped. Those are one-line fixes, against structural problems in A. Judged on clarity and tone only, not length, B wins on both and overall.
